items.title: Horse meat has been sold as minced beef or lamb in Australia, documents show
items.description: Government documents show hundreds of businesses operating in Australia have breached food safety laws, with one politician warning "you could be eating a minced horse".

items.title: GP says ban on puberty blockers is 'transphobic discrimination'
items.description: The fierce debate over puberty blockers has become a collision of science and politics. To try to address a fractured consensus, the federal government is attempting to lay the groundwork for a national standard.

items.title: Leadership spill as Carroll vies to replace Allan as Victorian Labor leader
items.description: Victorian Premier Jacinta Allan will face a leadership challenge at a meeting of Labor MPs this morning after Deputy Premier Ben Carroll said he would run for the top job.

items.title: Trump tips the balance towards China in trade war
items.description: China has the market sewn up in everything from solar panels to battery manufacturing and wind turbines. And now it is challenging America's commanding role in technology.

items.title: The troubling cost of the Norwegian salmon on your plate
items.description: Norway's salmon industry is a global behemoth 18 times the size of Tasmania's. But the country's success holds a warning for Australia.

items.title: Live: Harris leads Aussie medal sweep in 100m free as Dolphins dominate again
items.description: Australia is enjoying another wildly successful day at the Commonwealth Games, with Rose Davies claiming her nation's first athletics gold and the Dolphins sweeping the medals in two events in the pool.

items.title: Angus Taylor on the accident that changed his life
items.description: The Liberal leader opens about a balcony fall that left him with a broken back and altered the course of his life.

items.title: Australia should brace for war impact to get worse, Treasury warns
items.description: The federal government is yet to reveal whether it will extend the fuel excise discount, which is set to expire this week.

items.title: Power prices are finally falling. Experts say data centres could change that
items.description: Consumers should brace for hefty increases in the cost of generating electricity as data centres suck up vast quantities of power faster than new plants can be built, experts say.

items.title: Education as a tool to fight hate in focus at antisemitism royal commission
items.description: The Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion is continuing in Sydney, with witnesses to give evidence about ways to improve education and training to prevent hate.

items.title: Not satire: The Utopia-style regulations holding Australia back from building homes
items.description: A new report from the Productivity Commission has called on governments to embrace a "build mindset" to make housing more affordable.

items.title: 'Massive growth' of second-hand fashion apps in Australia
items.description: Resale app users are balancing convenience with overconsumption in the second-hand fashion conversation.

items.title: France and Spain race to curb wildfires before new heatwave arrives
items.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez highlighted the impact of climate change, saying the wildfires were "more ferocious" and "heatwaves more frequent".

items.title: Bill Oddie, member of The Goodies comedy series, dead at 85
items.description: British actor, comedian and broadcaster Bill Oddie, best known to Australian audiences as a member of the 1970s comedy trio The Goodies, has died aged 85, his agent has announced.

items.title: Boycotts and withdrawn funding 'part and parcel' of working in arts today
items.description: After the 2026 edition was subjected to political, community and commercial pressures, the Biennale of Sydney has announced a new artistic director: Singaporean curator Low Kee Hong.

items.title: Can't stop spending? These approaches can help curb impulse buying
items.description: If you'd rather be saving than shopping, but are struggling to switch gears, there are ways to change your habits.

items.title: ABC Places quiz: Where in the world are we?
items.description: Your challenge in the ABC Places quiz is to work out the location of 10 photos from around the world. Be warned; we might try to trick you.

items.title: Adverse decision on Salmon Tasmania advertisement overturned on appeal
items.description: Salmon Tasmania has won its appeal against an earlier decision that found one of its ad campaigns to be in breach of advertising standards.

items.title: Australia's first new oil refinery in decades touted for WA
items.description: The proposed facility would be built by Perdaman and be the first new large-scale petrol refinery built in Australia since the 1960s.

items.title: Baby still missing after bodies of woman and toddler found off SA coast
items.description: A baby under 12 months old remains missing after the bodies of a woman and a toddler were recovered from waters off the coast of Port MacDonnell in South Australia's South East, police say.

items.title: Australia's most disaster-hit state to opt out of AusAlert as government hails national test a success
items.description: The AusAlert system was tested today, with millions of devices receiving alerts, but many Australians reported issues and delays.

items.title: UK PM Burnham meets Zelenskyy and vows 'unwavering' support for Ukraine
items.description: Downing Street said the meeting was designed to underscore Britain's steadfast support for Ukraine.

items.title: Hanson 'disappointed' after losing racial discrimination appeal
items.description: One Nation leader Pauline Hanson loses an appeal against a court ruling which found she racially discriminated against Greens senator Mehreen Faruqi.

items.title: Previously unheard from survivors detail horrific abuse at Christian Brothers
items.description: As victims of child sexual abuse at the hands of Christian Brothers await compensation, they accuse those involved of stalling on payouts and abusing them all over again.

items.title: Netanyahu accuses New York's Mamdani of making Jews feel 'unsafe'
items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says he will still attend the United Nations General Assembly in September despite claiming the "rhetoric" of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani is making Jews feel "unsafe" in the city.
